slot.brief: Given initial and remaining concentration of a first-order reaction, count half-lives to find total time.

stem: The half-life of a first-order reaction is $12\ \text{min}$. How long does the concentration take to decrease from $0.48\ \text{mol L}^{-1}$ to $0.03\ \text{mol L}^{-1}$?

verdicts.working: The concentration decreases by a factor of 0.48/0.03 = 16 = 2^4, so 4 half-lives elapse: 4 × 12 = 48 min.

working:
$\dfrac{0.03}{0.48}=\dfrac{1}{16}=\left(\dfrac{1}{2}\right)^4$; hence $n=4$ half-lives.
$t=4\times12\ \text{min}=48\ \text{min}$

Independent check: The concentration decreases by a factor of 0.48/0.03 = 16 = 2^4, so 4 half-lives elapse: 4 × 12 = 48 min.
